confirmed.description: In the Kanka memory inset, pre-capture Nagoji has the wrong facial hair. He has a thin, short, straight moustache instead of the thick curled one, and visible stubble on his chin and jaw. The bible says CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN, with light stubble allowed only in captivity, and this is before his capture. The full-size present-day face in the same panel has the correct thick curled moustache, so the two faces side by side do not read as the same man. Turban, sash, gold stud and Kanka herself (black mare, brown bridle with brass fittings) match the sheets.
confirmed.evidence: page-06.png, crop about x 388-583, y 2205-2386. The moustache is a narrow dark bar that does not curl at the ends, and there is grey-dark stipple along the chin and jawline. Compare the same panel's close-up at about x 1000-1250, y 2250-2420.

verdict.reason:
The deviation is real but small, so I'm keeping it and downgrading it from major to minor. I zoomed into page-06.png (1838x2775), panel 6.5, around x 440-560, y 2260-2350. The memory-inset Nagoji is in left profile. His moustache is a short dark bar with a slight downward tip and no visible curl. There is also a faint grey shadow along the jaw and chin. The present-day close-up at about x 900-1150, y 2330-2420 has the full thick curled moustache and a clean chin. The bible line (CONTINUITY.md line 21-22: thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN, light stubble captivity only) does make this a technical miss, since the memory is set before his capture.

It is not major. At 300 DPI the inset face is only about 90 px from brow to chin, roughly 0.3 inch in print. At that size the jaw shadow reads as ordinary modelling, not stubble. A curl at the moustache tip would be about 1 mm, and the approved nagoji-v2 left-profile view itself shows only a slight upturn. The man in the inset still reads clearly as Nagoji: rust-red turban, gold ear stud, long black curls, cream tunic, red sash, same straight nose, pressed against the black mare. The reviewer's claim that the two faces do not read as the same man does not hold at print size. If panel 6.5 is regenerated for another reason, it is worth giving the inset a fuller, upturned moustache and a clean chin, but it does not need a redraw on its own.

confirmed.description: João's legs and footwear change from panel to panel. In 1.4, 2.3 and 4.2 he wears tall cuffed leather bucket boots over dark breeches, and in 4.2 he also has a crossed chest harness with a diamond buckle. In 4.4, 5.3, 6.4 and 8.3 he wears the approved-sheet look: knee breeches, cream stockings and low buckled shoes. Within page 4 the change happens between two consecutive panels of the same walk. Panel 1.4 is framed on his boots, so the reader is shown the wrong footwear first.
confirmed.evidence: 1.4 shows the tall cuffed boot on the bottom stair. In 2.3 the knee-high boot is raised to tap Nagoji. In 4.2 (left figure) he has knee-high boots and a crossed strap harness. In 4.4 (left figure) he has white stockings and low shoes, matching sheet 11-joao-v15.png.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this from crops of page 4. In 4.2, João (left figure, with the same face, jerkin and key ring) wears tall cuffed brown bucket boots over dark breeches. He also has a crossed chest strap with a diamond-shaped buckle, which is not on sheet 11-joao-v15.png and not in 2.2 or 2.3. In 4.4, the same man on the same walk wears cream stockings and low buckled shoes and has no strap, which matches the approved sheet. The two are consecutive beats of one walk: the script's 4.2 is the corridor walk with "João behind", and 4.3 is only a close-up of Nagoji's feet. The difference between boots and stockings is large and easy to see at print size. The continuity bible does not name his footwear, so nothing there allows the change. One part of the report needs softening. The script explicitly asks for "the gaoler's boots on the bottom stair" in 1.4 and has him tap Nagoji "with his boot" in 2.3. So the boots in 1.4 and 2.3 follow the script, and those panels are not errors on their own. The real problem is that one character's footwear flips from boots to shoes across the chapter, most visibly between 4.2 and 4.4. The fix is to pick one look (the script's boots, or the sheet's shoes) and make every panel match. I rated it major rather than blocker because his identity stays clear throughout: same face, jerkin, belt and keys. The change is localized to the costume.

confirmed.description: Duarte is seen from behind going down the stair, but his gold cross and chain are drawn on the back of his shoulder cape. The cross belongs on his chest.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of the right-hand figure in 2.1: the back of his grey head faces camera and he holds his hem in his right hand, yet a gold cross on a chain hangs down the middle of his back, over the cape.

verdict.reason: The problem is real, but I'm rating it minor rather than major. I zoomed into the priest in panel 2.1 (crop of the original render, about x 830-1110, y 420-880). He is plainly drawn from behind: we see the back of his grey head with only a sliver of cheek, the back of his collar and shoulder cape, the sash knot at his back, and his right hand holding the hem. From the back of his collar a thin gold chain runs down over the cape, and a gold cross hangs in the middle of his back. That is physically wrong. The bible puts "a small cross on a thin chain" on his cassock, which means the chest, and the script's 2.1 is a back view ("We do not see faces yet"), so neither source allows this. Why not major: at print scale the cross is only about 17x25 px at 300 DPI (roughly 1.5 x 2 mm) and the chain about 5 mm. It does show as a gold glint on the black cape, but the panel reads first as a priest going down the stair, and only a close reader will notice which side the cross is on. The fix is simple and needs no redraw: paint out the chain and cross, since a back view does not need them visible.

confirmed.description: How Nagoji is tied to the stool keeps changing during a single scene. In 5.3 João ties his wrists to the stool legs. In 6.2 his hands are free, one on his thigh and one on the stool edge, with rope only around the stool legs. In 6.4 a rope binds his chest and upper arms and his wrists are free at his sides. In 7.1 his hands rest free on his knees. In 7.4 his wrists are tied to the stool legs again.
confirmed.evidence: 6.2 zoom: no rope on his wrists or torso, and the left hand rests on the stool edge. 6.4 zoom: a rope wraps his chest and upper arms. 7.1 zoom: bandaged hands resting loose on his knees. 7.4 zoom: coiled rope ties each wrist down to a stool leg.

verdict.reason: I'm confirming this, but it is narrower than reported, and panel 6.4 is the real fault. Up close, 5.3, 6.2, 7.1 and 7.4 agree more than the reviewer said. In all four, coiled rope is wrapped over the linen bandages at both wrists. In 6.2 the reviewer said "no rope on his wrists", but the zoom shows thick rope coils on both wrists, with more coils on both stool legs. In 7.1 the wrists are also roped. The bottom of that panel cuts off below his hands, so a tie down to the stool legs could be out of frame. In 7.4 the rope runs from each wrist down to a stool leg, which matches the script's 5.3 line "wrists bound to its legs". Panel 6.4 breaks the pattern. It has a clear rope around the chest and upper arms, crossing the tunic, and only plain white bandages at the wrists with no rope. His near hand hangs down at the stool edge and the far hand rests on his thigh. Panel 6.2 sits just two panels above it on the same page, so the binding visibly changes mid-scene and contradicts the script. The chest rope is easy to see at print size. This is a localized prop and continuity error that does not change who the character is, so it is major, not a blocker. The fix is to redraw 6.4 with the wrists roped to the stool legs, as in 5.3 and 7.4, and no chest rope.

confirmed.description: The cellar setting contradicts itself on this page. The script says he is back 'chained in his place', meaning in the row from 1.1. In 9.1 he sits alone in a corner, with a large clay pot and basin at his right, empty wall and floor at his left, and a small table and stair beyond. In 9.3 he sits shoulder to shoulder with five chained prisoners in a continuous row.
confirmed.evidence: 9.1: a single figure chained to a wall ring, with no other prisoners anywhere in the wide panel. 9.3: prisoners crowd him on both sides, with their ankle chains linked in a line.

verdict.reason:
I'm confirming this as major. I cropped both panels, and they show two different setups on the same page.

- **Panel 9.1:** This is a wide panel that runs the full width of the page. Nagoji sits alone, and a long chain runs from a wall ring on the left to his ankle cuffs. A large clay pot and a basin sit to his left. To his right the wall and floor are bare out to a small table holding a jug, a keg and a cloth, then the lit stair and the window. There are no other prisoners anywhere in the frame. It reads as a solitary cell.
- **Panel 9.3:** The same man sits shoulder to shoulder in a chained row, with his ankle cuffs linked to the men on either side. The whisper comes along that line, and the dialogue ("They are gathering us for transport") depends on him being part of the group.

The script does not allow the solitary staging. It says 9.1 is "Back in the cellar. Nagoji chained in his place", which refers back to 1.1: fifteen men along the wall with their ankles linked by one iron bar. Page 1.1's render does show that row, with Nagoji at the near end.

The cast overrides don't excuse it either. They list only 'nagoji' for both 9.1 and 9.3, so they cover named characters only. Unnamed prisoners still fill 9.3.

This matters at print size. Because the panel is wide and the wall around him is empty, a reader will see a man alone in a different room. He then turns up in the group row two panels later, with no shift in scene to explain it.

It is not a blocker. The beat (eyes closed, calculating) and his identity both read correctly. The fix is local to 9.1: redraw it to show him in the chained row, as in 1.1 and 9.3, with the prisoners beside him visible or partly cropped. The wall ring, the separate pot and table, and the empty floor should go.

confirmed.description: The extent of Nagoji's bandages is inconsistent. The bible's chapter 1 row calls for bandaged hands and wrists, and the story needs his fingers hurt (the thumbnail wedge on 8.3). His hands are fully wrapped over the knuckles only in 3.1 and 9.1. Most other panels, including 9.3 right after the torture, show only a wrist band with bare, clean fingers. Page 9 contradicts itself: fully wrapped hands in 9.1, bare fingers in 9.3.
confirmed.evidence: 9.1 zoom: both hands wrapped to the knuckles. 9.3 zoom: only the wrists are wrapped, with clean bare fingers and thumbs. 6.2 and 7.1: cord-like wrist bands only, with bare hands.

verdict.reason: I confirmed the problem, but it is minor, not major. At 3x and 5x zoom, 9.1 shows both hands wrapped over the palms and knuckles in blood-stained linen with the fingertips out. That fits the bible (bandaged hands and wrists) and the script ("His hands are raw meat"). In 9.3, the same scene moments later, Nagoji has only narrow, clean cream cuffs at the wrists. The one hand you can see below a cuff is bare, clean skin, and the other is tucked under the dhoti fold. So page 9 does contradict itself, and 9.3 falls short of the bible's "bandaged hands". I rate it minor for three reasons. First, both panels still read as bandaged wrists at print size; in 9.3 the cuffs are about 0.3 inch wide and the hands are mostly hidden. Second, the key injured-hands beat is carried by 9.1, which is drawn correctly, and 9.3's story beat is the whisper, not the hands. Third, the wider claim is weak. 1.1 and 3.1 show full hand wraps, and the "cord-like" bands in 6.2 and 7.1 (plus 7.4 and 8.5, where he is a small background figure) are hard to tell apart from the wrist ropes script 5.3 calls for, and too small to matter in print. The fix is a polish pass: match 9.3's wraps to 9.1 (stained linen over the palms and knuckles).

confirmed.description: The bottom two panels get narrower in steps, so the page's side edges are ragged. The key staging beat 5.3 (Nagoji seated and bound, Joao checking the knot, Duarte standing back) is shrunk into a strip barely three quarters of full width. The figures are about 0.4 in tall at print size and the knot is hard to read. This is a regression: in r6, 5.3 filled the full row width.
confirmed.evidence: Measured on the 300 DPI render: 5.1 spans x=148 to 1688 (the live area every full-width panel uses). 5.2 spans x=241 to 1596 (93 px cream inset each side). 5.3 spans only x=344 to 1492 (196 px, about 0.65 in, of cream on each side). The r6 page-05 had 5.3 flush at 148 to 1688. On page 1 of the approved standard, every panel is flush to both margins.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on the r7 page-05.png at 300 DPI. My own column scan gives the same numbers: 5.1 spans x=148 to 1688, 5.2 spans 241 to 1596, and 5.3 spans only 344 to 1492. That leaves 5.3 at 1148 px wide (about 3.8 in) against the 1540 px (5.1 in) live area, with about 0.65 in of cream on each side. The regression claim also holds. In r6, 5.3 was flush at 148 to 1688; only 5.2 was inset (219 to 1618). The row heights in LAYOUT.json (78 and 91.5 pt) are unchanged, so the new 5.3 frame (page-05-panel-03-v04, about 3:1) was letterboxed into a row that expects about 4:1. On the full page the three panels step inward, which is easy to see and looks like a mistake, not a design choice. The chapter's own standard is flush panels: pages 1 and 6 are flush, and REVIEW.md item 19 records page 6 being adjusted specifically for flush edges. The script does not excuse this. It calls 5.2 an 'Insert', which could justify 5.2's small inset, but 5.3 is a 'Narrow strip', meaning a short full-width band, not a narrower one. One part of the report is overstated: the figures are not 0.4 in tall. Seated Nagoji is about 285 px (0.95 in) and the crouching Joao about 0.83 in. At that size the staging still reads: Nagoji bound on the stool with his ankle irons linked, Joao's hands at the wrist rope, and Duarte standing back. So the beat is not missing, and this does not rise to blocker. It is a clearly wrong, localized layout error that loses about 25% of the panel's width on the page's key staging beat. The fix is to re-fit or extend the 5.3 frame to the full-width row, not to redraw it.

confirmed.description: The panel art does not fill its frame. A white band runs the full width of the panel's bottom edge, between the art's own black edge line and the outer panel border. The result is a doubled, broken frame that is visible at print size. Carried over unchanged from r6.
confirmed.evidence: Pixel scan at x=750 to 850: art ends at row 1521, a black rule runs from 1522 to 1525, pure white (value about 252) from 1526 to 1536 (11 px, about 0.9 mm), then the outer border from 1537 to 1539. Visible in the display render as a white line under Nagoji's eyes and moustache along the bottom of the frame.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 7, panel 7.3 (the Nagoji eyes close-up with the Godavari caption). In /Users/roshanvenugopal/Documents/github/nagoji/output/comic-v15-full-redo/chapters/ch01-v2/renders/r7/page-07.png (1838x2775), pixel columns at x=300, 800 and 1500 all show the same thing. The art ends at row 1521. A black rule belonging to the art runs from 1522 to 1525. Near-white (252 to 254) runs from 1526 to 1536, which is 11 px, about 0.9 mm at 300 DPI. The outer panel border runs from 1537 to 1539, then the page cream (240). The left and right edges are clean: only the outer border, with art right up against it. The top edge is also clean. So the defect is only along the bottom, across the full panel width. You can see it without zooming in the downscaled page view: a white strip with a doubled black frame under Nagoji's moustache. None of the other panels on the page has it. The cause is in the source art. The last rows of /Users/roshanvenugopal/Documents/github/nagoji/output/comic-v15-full-redo/chapters/ch01-v2/frames/page-07-panel-03-v15-r2.png (2079x756) are already white (253), so the generated image came with its own border and a white margin, and compositing kept both. Neither the script nor the bible allows for this, and at almost 1 mm across the full width it is not too slight to matter in print. Severity is major, not blocker: it is a localized production defect that hides no story beat or identity, and it can be fixed by re-cropping or rescaling the frame source so the art fills the panel, with no redraw needed.

confirmed.description: The script says 'Back on his face, present again, answering' for the chapter's thesis line (the 'better powder' line, which pays off in ch28). The art is a medium-long shot of Nagoji sitting on the stool at the right third of the panel. His face is small and he is looking up and away toward the ceiling, not answering Duarte. The close-up face beat is lost.
confirmed.evidence: page-07.png panel 4. The figure fills only the right third. His head is about 90px tall in a 1838px-wide page, and he gazes up to the upper right while the balloon fills the left two thirds.

verdict.reason: I confirm it. The script for 7.4 says "Back on his face, present again, answering." Nothing in CONTINUITY or the cast overrides allows a wide shot here. The r7 page-07.png panel 4 is a medium-long full-figure shot instead. Nagoji sits roped to the stool in the right third, and the left two thirds hold the balloon and an empty tool table. In the zoomed crop (x 1050-1350, y 1650-1900) his head is about 100px tall on the 2775px page, around 0.37 in at print size. His head and eyes turn up toward the upper right. Duarte was set up screen-left in 7.2, facing right, so Nagoji is looking away from the man he is answering. Coming straight after 7.3 ("He is not in the room"), that upward look away reads as still distracted, not "present again." It weakens the chapter's thesis line, which pays off in ch28. The shot also nearly repeats 7.1's framing, so the page loses its planned move from the wide shot to the close-up. The speaker is still clear (the tail points to him), the lettering is fine and the face is recognizable, so the beat is not missing. That makes this a major, localized framing and eyeline error, not a blocker. Fix: redraw 7.4 as a head-and-shoulders or close-up of Nagoji with his eyes level and aimed screen-left toward Duarte.

confirmed.description: How Nagoji is bound changes from panel to panel during the interrogation, against 5.3, 7.1 and 7.4, where his wrists are roped to the stool legs. In 6.2 he sits in a chair with armrests and his wrists are tied to the arms. In 6.4 a rope is wound around his torso and his arms are pulled behind him. In 8.5, mid-torture, he sits untied with his hands resting in his lap, calm and nearly smiling. The reader loses track of the restraint the scene depends on.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of page-06.png (850,1000)-(1200,1370) shows a chair with arms and wrists roped to the armrests. Crop (380,1700)-(750,2130) shows ropes across his chest and upper arms. Crop of page-08.png (1250,1560)-(1690,1960) shows him unbound on the stool with hands folded in his lap. Crop of page-07.png (950,1680)-(1350,2170) shows the scripted setup, wrists roped to the stool legs.

verdict.reason:
Partly confirmed. The 6.2 part is wrong, but 6.4 and 8.5 do break the restraint.

- **6.2 is fine.** A zoomed crop of page-06 (850,1000)-(1200,1370) shows the same wooden stool with rope wound round its legs, not a chair with armrests. His hands rest on the edge of the seat with rope wraps over the bandaged wrists. That matches 7.1, and it fits the script ("bound to the stool").
- **6.4 is wrong.** In crop (380,1680)-(760,2130) a new rope is wound round his chest and upper arms, with his right arm pulled back to the seat edge. His left hand lies loose on his thigh. No wrist is roped to a stool leg. This contradicts 5.3 (João tying his wrist to the leg) and 7.4, where both wrists are clearly roped to the stool legs. The torso rope then disappears in 7.1. The figure is large in the panel, so a reader will see it even at print size.
- **8.5 is wrong.** Crop (1270,1580)-(1500,1900) of page-08 shows him on the stool with both bandaged hands clasped loosely in his lap, no rope visible anywhere, and a relaxed pose during the torture beat. The script does ask for him "blurred, in the background", so the calm pose and the missing ropes are the only problems in this panel.
- **8.3** shows João holding his hand out from the stool. The wedge scene needs that access, so it is acceptable.

This is a continuity error inside one scene, confined to two panels, like a costume error. That makes it major, not a blocker.

refuted.description: Nagoji wears metal finger rings on both bandaged hands. The bandaged hands are what this panel is about (Duarte's eyes go to them). Neither the Nagoji sheet nor the bible gives him rings, a stripped prisoner would not keep them, and no other panel in the chapter shows any.
refuted.reason: Refuted: the detail is too small to matter in print. On page 3, panel 3.1, each bandaged hand is only about 60 px wide at 300 DPI, roughly 0.2 inch on the printed page. At 8 to 12x zoom (crops of x 900-960 and 970-1040, y 600-660) there are thin pale grey bands around a few fingers, and one on the right hand has a small highlight. But each band is about 4-5 px, around 0.015 inch at print size, the same off-white as the linen, and runs into the wrap. At native panel size and at print size they read as loose strips of bandage wound round the fingers, not jewelry. Nothing at reading size tells a reader these are rings. The beat the script asks for is still clear: Duarte's eyes go to the stained, bandaged hands. That fits the bible's chapter 1 row ('bandaged hands and wrists'). Rings on a prisoner would not be allowed, but the art does not show them clearly enough to count, so under the if-uncertain rule this is refuted.

refuted.description: Nagoji in the background does not follow on from the torture in 8.3. He is sharp rather than blurred (the script asks for blurred), sits relaxed and unbound with a slight smile, and is in a different part of the room: against a wall between hanging chains, next to the door, with a small table behind him. In 8.3 he is on the stool in the middle of the room with João working on his hand.
refuted.reason:
I zoomed into page 8, panels 8.3 and 8.5, and the art does not support the complaint.
(1) Focus: at 1.5x to 5x zoom, Nagoji in 8.5 is clearly soft, with a shallow depth of field. His face, hair and bandages smear at high zoom, while Duarte's and João's hands in the foreground stay crisp. That is the "blurred, in the background" the script asks for, just not heavily blurred.
(2) Not "unbound": iron cuffs on both ankles, with chain between them, are plainly visible. That matches the ch1 bible row (bandaged hands and wrists, ankle irons, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, barefoot, hair loose) and matches 8.3, where his hands are also not tied because João is holding one.
(3) "Faintly smiling": at 5x the face is too soft to read a smile. It looks neutral and watchful.
(4) Location: 8.5 is a reverse angle taken from the brazier. In 8.3 the brazier is up and to the left of the stool, and the table and door are to its right, so looking from the brazier toward Nagoji puts a door and a table behind him on the right. That is what 8.5 shows. It also makes sense that he is alone on the stool, because João has stepped away to reach for the brazier. The only new set detail is the wall chains in place of the ceiling ropes, which is too small to matter at print size.
(5) Clean bandages: the bandages are just as clean in 8.3, so this is not a break between the two panels.
That leaves only a subjective point: his upright, composed posture. The script does not ask for visible agony here, and its "mind floats free" direction allows it. I count it as polish at most, not a major continuity error.

refuted.description: The wince the script calls for ('Draw the wince. It matters.') is missing. Duarte's eyes are almost shut and aimed down at his own lap, not at Nagoji's bandaged hands, and his face looks calm and sorrowful. Nagoji is holding his bandaged hands up and looking down at them himself. That reads as a cowed man tending his wounds, which undercuts the page's purpose of showing Nagoji is not cowed.
refuted.reason:
I'm refuting this. I zoomed in on panel 3.1 of page-03.png, at crops (620,370)-(860,560) and (880,420)-(1150,700) in the 1838x2775 original.

1. **The wince is there, just restrained.** Duarte's face is not calm. His brows are pinched, his forehead is creased and the corners of his mouth turn down. That reads as a pained, troubled reaction. Tucking his hands into his sleeves follows the script ("His fingers twitch inside his sleeves").

2. **His gaze fits the script.** His head is angled steeply down and to the right, toward Nagoji's raised hands, which sit just below and to his right. The claim that he is looking at his own lap is not clear from the art.

3. **Nagoji is not cowed.** His face is a hard scowl with a furrowed brow and a set jaw. The script gives Nagoji no action in 3.1, and holding up the bandaged hands helps the beat, because it shows the reader what Duarte is reacting to. Panels 3.2 and 3.3 then carry the level gaze and the defiant reply as scripted.

4. **The rest is too slight.** The only remaining gap is that the expression is a subdued grimace rather than a sharp flinch. At print size that difference hardly shows, and the panel still gets across what the wince is for: Duarte is visibly disturbed by the torture.

At most, deepening the wince would be optional polish.

Side note, not part of this claim: João is drawn in the panel and his balloon tail points at him, though the script marks him "(off)" and the cast overrides leave him out of page-03-panel-01.

refuted.description: The script wants Nagoji's face in profile, lit by the red glow from a dark doorway, as the setup for the page turn. The art is instead a wide shot of all three figures walking. Nagoji's small profile is lit by warm corridor light, not the red glow, and Duarte stands between him and the door. The doorway itself is a flat, solid red slab, not a dark opening with a glow coming from inside.
refuted.reason: I looked at the bottom panel of page 4 at full size and zoomed in on Nagoji's face and the doorway. The main claims don't hold up. (1) Lighting: Nagoji is in profile facing right, toward the door. His forehead, nose, lips, chin and the front of his tunic have warm orange-red light coming from the right, from the doorway. The back of his head is in shadow. So he is not lit from the left by the corridor torches; the glow from the doorway does reach his face, as the script asks. (2) Doorway: it is not a flat solid slab. It is an open doorway with a stone frame and a lit threshold step. Inside is glowing red haze with a faint shape in it, and red light spills onto the step and the floor. It reads as light coming from a room we can't see, so the room is still withheld for the page turn. (3) Staging: showing all three figures, with Duarte leading and Joao behind, was a deliberate fix from the previous round. chapters/ch01-v2/REVIEW.md, issue 14, says Duarte should lead and Joao follow into the doorway to keep the escort from 4.2 consistent. The script line for 4.4 does not rule out other figures and does not demand a tight close-up. The one real difference is that the shot is wider than the script suggests, so Nagoji's face is small. But his profile reads clearly, faces the glowing door and catches its light. The beat and the page-turn setup work, so this is too slight to count as a major problem.

refuted.description: This is the planted hesitation beat, which the script says 'the reader must remember in chapter 24'. It has been flattened into two nearly identical half-width frames. 8.1 does not show 'his jaw works, as if he is chewing words'; it is only a downcast look. 8.2's nod is just a slightly lower head tilt in the same composition, so the two panels read as a duplicate rather than as a struggle followed by a decision.
refuted.reason:
Refuted as a major problem. I zoomed into both frames on page 8 (top row, x 150-915 and 922-1687, y 360-630, with 4x crops of the face and mouth). Panels 8.1 and 8.2 do share the same camera, torch, wall and cross. That is deliberate. Repeating a frame with one small change is the standard comics way to stage a silent pause and then a decision, and the script's own change table asks for exactly this: "Two wordless panels, 8.1 and 8.2, so the reader sees the hesitation and remembers it."

The change between the panels is real and shows up at page size:
- 8.1: eyes open and cast down to the side, brows knit, lips pressed tight with the corners pulled down. A single still cannot show a jaw moving, and this pressed-mouth tension is the usual way to draw "chewing words he cannot swallow."
- 8.2: eyelids closed and the head dipped lower, which is a clear "small, weary nod."

8.2 matches its script line. 8.1 gives Duarte a full panel as the script asks ("hold on him for a full panel" means a whole panel, not a full-width one). The two frames read as struggle, then yielding. The low mean pixel difference (about 13/255) is simply what an intended held-frame repeat looks like; it does not mean the beat is missing.

Only a polish note is left: the artist could push the jaw clench a little harder in 8.1 (a tighter mouth or a visible jaw muscle) so the hesitation reads more strongly next to 8.2. That is minor and does not need a redraw.

refuted.description: The key-ring inset shows a red coat with white facings behind the belt. That reads as a British redcoat, which the continuity bible forbids for Portuguese guards. The guard inset beside it (tricornes, crossed white belts, muskets) adds to the 18th-century British or colonial-American look.
refuted.reason: The art has the red detail, but it is too small to make the guards read as British redcoats. In the key-ring inset (page-09.png, x about 820-925, y 945-1415), the right edge shows a thin strip of red cloth with a white band and one brass button. The strip is about 40 px of a 375 px wide inset, roughly 3 mm on the printed page. I checked it at print scale (the page shrunk to one-third) and it shows up only as a flash of red at the edge, with no coat shape, cuff or lapel to recognise. The garment that fills the inset matches Joao's continuity row: a brown jerkin with brass buttons, a cream shirt, a wide leather belt and an iron key ring. The guard inset next to it shows brown waistcoats over cream shirts, not red coats, so no guard on the page is in red. Tricornes, crossed buff belts, muskets and boots are standard European infantry kit for 1738, and Portuguese troops wore them too. The bible forbids only British redcoats and Dutch blue-coats, and the brown, cream and buff here are neither. The script's 9.2 beats (guards at the door, key ring, boots on the stair, bucket) are all present and readable. At most this is a minor fix: recolour the red strip brown or dark, so the gaoler's inset has no stray red.

minors.description: Duarte's face drifts from his sheet. It is broad and fleshy with jowls, and the hair is wind-tousled and blond-grey. The sheet and other panels (2.2, 6.1, 8.1, 8.6) show a gaunt, long, narrow face with hollow cheeks and neatly swept-back grey curls. The cassock and cross make him recognisable, but this face reads as a different older man in the panel that should carry his wince.
minors.evidence: page-03.png, crop about x 652-846, y 368-527. Compare 10-father-duarte-v15.png (expressions row) and page-06.png, panel 6.1 (about x 1000-1330, y 370-720).

minors.description: Duarte is heavier and more rugged here, with a thick jaw and fleshy nose, than his gaunt sheet face. In 7.2 his eyes are clearly dark brown, but the bible and script (2.2) give him grey eyes. This is the close-up where he lowers his voice to Nagoji, so the eye colour shows.
minors.evidence: page-07.png, 7.2 eye crop about x 652-860, y 832-971: brown irises. 7.5 face about x 222-1082, y 2212-2540: broad jaw and nose, fuller cheeks than the sheet.

minors.description: Duarte's costume is inconsistent. In 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.5, 4.2 and 6.1 he wears a shoulder cape (pellegrina) over his cassock. In 5.3, 7.2, 8.1, 8.2, 8.3 and 8.6 he wears the plain cassock with no cape, as on his sheet. The switch happens inside the interrogation scene, between 6.1 and 7.2.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, 6.1: a cape falls over the shoulders and upper arms (about x 980-1360, y 520-760). page-07.png, 7.2: plain cassock shoulder with no cape (about x 150-800, y 870-1200). 10-father-duarte-v15.png shows no cape in any view.

minors.description: João's footwear changes from panel to panel. In 1.4, 2.3 and 4.2 he wears tall cuffed leather bucket boots. In 4.4, 5.3 and 6.4 he wears white stockings with buckled shoes, as on his sheet. 4.2 and 4.4 are consecutive panels of the same walk.
minors.evidence: page-04.png, 4.2: tall brown boots at about x 480-560, y 1310-1390 (João, far left). 4.4: white stockings and low shoes at about x 400-640, y 2380-2500. 11-joao-v15.png: stockings and buckled shoes.

minors.description: There is a Nagoji look-alike in the chained line: a prisoner with the same kit of curly black hair, thick curled moustache and clean chin. In the establishing panel meant to pick out Nagoji, a duplicate face dilutes the read. Other prisoners should get beards, grey hair or a different moustache.
minors.evidence: page-01.png: the prisoner just left of the grey-bearded elder, about x 740-860, y 610-720 at native resolution (display x 575, y 480).

minors.description: In the chapter's final close-up, Nagoji's face carries a crackled, wet-plastic skin texture across the forehead and cheeks (an upscaler artifact), and his nose is broad and bulbous. Together they make him look much older and rougher than the 25-year-old on the sheet, with its straight nose. He is still recognisable from the hair, stud and moustache ends.
minors.evidence: page-09.png, crop about x 666-1054, y 1997-2275: worm-like crazing on the forehead and under the eyes. Compare the clean skin in panels 1.3 and 2.4 and on nagoji-v2.png.

minors.description: This is outside the identity lens but clearly visible. Under the art in panel 7.3 there is an empty white strip inside a doubled bottom border. A grey stone fragment also sits in front of Nagoji's jaw at the lower-left corner.
minors.evidence: page-07.png: a white band across about x 243-1595, y 1523-1537 under the moustache. A grey block overlaps the lower-left of the face at about x 243-280, y 1485-1520.

minors.description: Duarte's short shoulder cape (pellegrina) appears and disappears. The approved sheet 10-father-duarte-v15.png shows a plain cassock with a cincture and no cape. The cape is drawn in 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.5, 4.2 and 6.1, but not in 4.4, 5.3, 7.2, 8.3 or 8.6, so his outline changes within page 4 and between pages 6 and 7.
minors.evidence: 4.2: the black cape over his shoulders ends at the elbow. 4.4, the next panel of the same walk: a plain cassock with standing collar and sash, and no cape.

minors.description: The torture table moves across the room within the page. In 6.1 and 6.2 it stands against the back wall to the left of the stool, with the brazier to Nagoji's right and the door at far right. In 6.4 the table stands at far right in front of the door, and João picks up the tongs there. The brazier stays centred and the door stays on the right, so this is not a reverse angle.
minors.evidence: 6.2: table left of Nagoji, brazier right, door far right. 6.4: Nagoji far left, brazier centre, table at far right against the door.

minors.description: The table's position relative to Nagoji flips between panels on the same page. In 7.1 the tool table is just to his right, between him and the brazier. In 7.4 the table is at the far left of the frame and there is only open floor between him and the brazier.
minors.evidence: 7.1: table directly behind and right of the stool, brazier beyond it. 7.4: table cut off at the left edge, a large gap to Nagoji, and the brazier and door to his right with no table.

minors.description: João's light source changes during the same descent. He carries a flaming torch in 2.1 and a glass-paned lantern in 2.3.
minors.evidence: 2.1: a raised torch in his right hand. 2.3: a lit lantern hanging from his right hand, and no torch.

minors.description: Duarte's torch disappears during the walk. He holds a lit torch in 4.2 and has empty hands in 4.4, the next beat of the same walk.
minors.evidence: 4.2: torch raised in his left hand at the right edge. 4.4: both hands empty at his sides as he reaches the red-lit doorway.

minors.description: Where Nagoji sits changes between pages 2 and 3 of the same scene. In 2.2 and 2.3 he sits on a raised stone ledge with prisoners on either side. In 3.1 he sits on the floor with no neighbouring prisoners, a chain runs to a wall ring, and a table and bucket are behind Duarte.
minors.evidence: 2.3: Nagoji on a stone step or ledge between two slumped prisoners. 3.1: Nagoji cross-legged on the flagstones, with only Duarte and João near him.

minors.description: The caption points to the calluses on Duarte's right hand, but the open right palm shows scattered ink blots and no calluses.
minors.evidence: Zoom of his extended right palm (screen-left): dark spots on the palm and fingertips, with no thickened callus pads at the base of the fingers.

minors.description: Props in the chamber change between panels. The table in 5.1 holds only four pincers, two hammers, wedges and a small tong set. The close-up in 5.2 adds three iron manacles, folded cloth, a coil of rope, a box, a bowl, a jug and extra mallets. The brazier is a wide basket on a low tripod against the back wall in 5.1, but a slim tall pedestal brazier next to the door in 5.3.
minors.evidence: 5.2: manacles at the far left of the table, and a cloth, box and jug at the back. 5.1: none of those on the table. 5.3: a tall black pedestal brazier at right beside the door.

minors.description: The brazier in 8.5 is a large waist-high pan heaped with glowing coals, which does not match the slim basket-on-tripod brazier in 8.3 and 8.6.
minors.evidence: 8.5: a broad iron pan spans the lower right quarter of the panel. 8.3 and 8.6: a small round basket brazier on thin legs.

minors.description: The key-ring inset shows a red coat panel with white tape at the right edge. The bible's standing rules say Portuguese guards must not read as British redcoats.
minors.evidence: Zoom of inset 2: to the right of the brown coat and belt is a red coat front with a white tape stripe and a brass fitting.

minors.description: The ledger does not match the scripted beat, where the entry has just been written and the ink is still wet. The quill is poised over the blank right-hand page, while the entry '17 prisioneiro marata' sits on the left page in a clean printed italic, not wet handwriting.
minors.evidence: 1.2: the pen tip rests on the empty right page, and the typeset line sits mid-left page.

minors.description: A white strip runs along the bottom of the panel inside its border. The art does not fill the frame.
minors.evidence: 7.3: a blank white band about 10 px high sits between the image's bottom edge and the black panel border.

minors.description: The guard in the key-ring inset has a bold red band edged with a white stripe at the right edge. It reads as a British redcoat's cuff or coat turnback with white lace. Under the standing rule, Portuguese guards must not read as redcoats. The other guards in 9.2 wear brown waistcoats, so this inset is inconsistent with them.
minors.evidence: page-09.png, approx x 830-917, y 950-1150 (right edge of the second inset, behind the brass flask): a saturated red fabric panel with a white stripe beside a brown coat with brass buttons. Crop reviewed at 1.5x.

minors.description: In the Kanka memory vignette, the rider's red sash breaks up into red droplets and flecks inside the black-and-white ink-splatter edge. The panel comes right after 'We shot it' in 6.4, so at page scale the red spatter beside the horse can read as a spray of blood. The standing rule forbids blood. The dissolve should use only the neutral black and white splatter.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, approx x 560-690, y 2390-2510: red and pink droplets mixed into the splatter below the sash, visible as a red smear at normal page view. Crop reviewed at 3x.

minors.description: The ledger text '17 prisioneiro marata' is a flat, clean digital serif italic laid over the art. It ignores the curve and perspective of the page, and it looks pasted on, not written with a quill. It also sits on the LEFT page while the quill is writing on the blank RIGHT page, so the scripted 'ink is still wet' entry does not look like the one being written.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, approx x 290-575, y 1380-1420: typeset text floating level across the left page. The pen nib is at approx x 700-760, y 1450-1490 on the empty right page.

minors.description: The generated art has its own frame baked in along the bottom: a black rule plus a white strip about 10 px tall, sitting inside the real panel border. The panel shows a visible double border and an empty white band under Nagoji's face.
minors.evidence: page-07.png, full panel width (x approx 243-1597): art stops with a black line at y 1521-1525, white fill (RGB ~253) at y 1526-1536, then the real panel border at y 1537-1539. Pixel-sampled.

minors.description: Several frame and gutter problems on page 3. First, 3.1 has the same doubled-border defect as 7.3, only thinner: a white hairline sits inside the bottom frame. Second, 3.2 is inset from both margins and carries a visibly heavier doubled frame than its neighbours. Third, the gutters jump from tight to wide partway down the page.
minors.evidence: 3.1 bottom at x=800: black at 905/906, white at 908/909, then the outer border at 910 to 912. 3.2 spans x=190 to 1647 against the 148 to 1688 live area. Gutters measured: 3.1 to 3.2 is 12 px, 3.2 to 3.3 is 6 px, 3.3 to 3.4 is 54 px, 3.4 to 3.5 is 55 px.

minors.description: Joao's off-panel tail in 7.5 stops short of the frame. It ends in empty wall inside the panel instead of running to the border the way the off-panel tail in 8.6 does. The 7.5 panel is also inset from the margins, and the gutters on page 7 are several times wider than on pages 4 to 6.
minors.evidence: The 7.5 tail tip is at about x=1564; the panel's right border is at x=1622, so there is a gap of about 55 px. The panel spans x=215 to 1622 against the 148 to 1688 live area, and 7.3 spans 240 to 1596. Gutters: 7.1 to 7.2 and 7.2 to 7.3 are 53 px each, 7.3 to 7.4 and 7.4 to 7.5 are 39 px each. Pages 4 to 6 use 6 to 7 px.

minors.description: Bad line breaks leave single words stranded. In 7.2 the break splits the key phrase 'For me.' so that 'me.' sits alone on its own line. In 7.4, 'you.' is stranded the same way. The same happens with 'read.' in 6.3.
minors.evidence: 7.2 balloon reads 'Tell me this at least, Nagoji. Not for the Viceroy. For / me. / Do you believe...'. 7.4 reads '...I leave Him to the Brahmins and to / you. / He seems to favour...'. 6.3 reads 'My horse does not / read.' inside a balloon with a large empty right half.

minors.description: Joao's three-line balloon is too short for its copy. The first line sits almost against the top of the outline while the side margins are generous, so the lettering looks crammed.
minors.evidence: Zoomed crop at x=780 to 1200, y=1690 to 1800: the top of the 'Y' in 'Your horse is dead. We shot it' is about 10 px below the balloon outline. The left and right margins are 40 px or more.

minors.description: The captions in 4.2 and 4.3 are jammed into the top-right corner of their panels, almost touching the frame. On the same page, the 4.1 caption and the approved page 1 captions keep a clear margin of art. Panel 4.3 is also inset from both margins.
minors.evidence: The right edge of the 4.2 caption box meets the panel border (x=1688) with about 5 px of art or less on top and right. The 4.3 caption is about 7 to 8 px from the top border and 7 px from the right border (x=1607). The 4.1 caption sits about 14 px from the top and 22 px from the left. Panel 4.3 spans x=230 to 1607 against the 148 to 1688 live area.

minors.description: Two panels on page 8 are inset from the margins, while 8.1/8.2, 8.3 and 8.5 are flush. This gives the page a ragged left and right edge, unlike the approved page 1.
minors.evidence: 8.4 spans x=235 to 1601 and 8.6 spans x=193 to 1644. The live area used by 8.3 and 8.5 is 148 to 1688.

minors.description: The script calls for the final caption, 'Storms do not ask permission.', to be separate and weighted. It is lettered exactly like the three captions above it (same font, size and weight, same plain white box), so the chapter's closing line gets no extra emphasis. The 'Ships meant movement' box is also padded to roughly twice the height its two lines need.
minors.evidence: Script 9.4: 'CAPTION (separate, weighted): Storms do not ask permission.' In the 9.4 crop, the bottom-right box uses the same DIN Condensed weight and size as 'They had forgotten the simplest lesson of the Deccan monsoon.' The first caption box is about 165 px tall for two text lines.

minors.description: The prisoner's line in 9.3 is a whisper passing along the chained line, but it is lettered in a standard solid speech balloon with no whisper treatment. Separately, panel 9.1 starts noticeably lower on the page than the first panel on every other page, and the gutters between rows vary widely.
minors.evidence: The 9.3 balloon has a solid black outline, identical to the normal speech balloons. The top of 9.1 is at y=406; on pages 2 to 8 the first panel starts at y=358 to 364. Gutters on page 9: 55 px, 22 px, 33 px.

minors.description: Three lettering and layout problems on page 2. The left caption in 2.2 is about twice the height its single line needs. The text in the 2.3 balloon is pushed to the left, leaving the right half empty. Panel 2.4 is inset from both margins, so the page's left and right edges don't line up.
minors.evidence: 2.2 left caption: one line of text floats in a box about 150 px tall. 2.3 balloon spans about x=955 to 1540, but the text only runs from about 990 to 1280. 2.4 spans x=176 to 1661 while 2.1 to 2.3 span 148 to 1688.

minors.description: The script and the audited cast list both treat Joao's line in 3.1 as off-panel. The render draws Joao inside the panel and points an on-panel tail at him instead of using an off-panel tail.
minors.evidence: Script 3.1: 'JOÃO (off): Two days. He still insists he is only a horseman.' CHAPTER-01-CAST-OVERRIDES.json lists page-03-panel-01 as ['duarte','nagoji'] only. In the render, the right balloon's tail ends on a visible, bearded Joao at the far right.

minors.description: The chapter title 'Dungeons of Goa' is repeated at full title size at the top of every continuation page. It uses about an inch of each page and makes each page look like a chapter opener. The same template is in r6; flagged so it can be a deliberate decision.
minors.evidence: The same Georgia Bold title, centred at about y=300 (native), appears on pages 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9, identical to the chapter-opening title on page 1.

minors.description: The script asks for Nagoji in three-quarter back view, withholding his face until the 1.3 close-up, and for a window light that 'is failing'. Instead he looks back over his shoulder straight at the reader with his face fully lit, which spends the 1.3 reveal early. The slit window throws a bright, strong shaft of light.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-01.png (1150,500)-(1700,1070): his full face with eye contact, moustache and ear stud is clearly visible and lit by a bright window beam.

minors.description: The quill is writing on the blank right-hand page, while the entry '17 prisioneiro marata' sits on the left-hand page in clean typeset italic. The 'ink still wet, being written now' beat reads instead as a pre-printed label with no connection to the pen.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-01.png (150,1080)-(920,1600): the pen nib rests on an empty right page, and the entry is centred on the left page in a uniform serif typeface.

minors.description: The bells, which the script wants 'rendered as sound, not object', appear as two tiny grey clip-art eighth-note glyphs floating beside the water drop. They read as a UI music icon, not church bells.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-01.png (150,2170)-(1700,2500): two small grey eighth notes at about x=600, y=150 within the crop.

minors.description: Duarte is seen from behind, but his cross and chain hang on his back over the shoulder cape.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-02.png (140,360)-(1700,880): the back of Duarte's grey head faces the camera, and the gold cross dangles at his upper back.

minors.description: The script says 'Draw the calluses on his right hand clearly', and the caption depends on them. The right hand is shown open palm-up but only has ink dots, with no readable calluses at print size. The panel also adds Nagoji and João, though the cast list has Duarte alone. Nagoji sits on a raised stone ledge here and in 2.3, but on the floor in the chained line in 1.1 and 3.1.
minors.evidence: Zoom of page-02.png (700,1260)-(850,1420): the palm is smooth apart from blue ink spots. In the full panel Nagoji is at the far left on a stone bench, and João stands behind Duarte at the right.

minors.description: João's line is scripted as off-panel ('JOÃO (off)'), but he stands in frame at the upper right with an in-panel tail. The cast list for 3.1 is Duarte and Nagoji only.
minors.evidence: page-03.png panel 1: João is standing against the right wall, and the 'Two days...' balloon tail points to his head.

minors.description: Duarte's off-panel tail comes in from the right edge, but Duarte was set up on screen left in 3.1 and Nagoji's eyeline is to the camera or the left. Nagoji is also leaning on his forearms as if at a table or ledge, where in 3.1 he sat cross-legged on the floor.
minors.evidence: page-03.png panel 2: the balloon tail exits the top-right corner. His forearms rest on a horizontal surface across the bottom of the frame.

minors.description: The script asks for his mouth 'cracked and rust-dark', but the lips are smooth, full and healthy, so the mark of mistreatment is lost.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-03.png (600,1310)-(1500,1830): the lips are glossy and unbroken, with no cracks or dried blood.

minors.description: The binding ropes from the ceiling ring end in decorative gold tassels, like a chandelier or bell-pull, which softens the menace the reveal was built for. The script's heat shimmer above the brazier is also not visible. The same tasselled ropes repeat in 6.1-6.4, 7.1, 7.2, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.6.
minors.evidence: page-05.png panel 1: golden ropes with tasselled ends hang from the ring at the centre top, and the brazier flame shows no distortion.

minors.description: The script sets the memory on 'a winter morning'. The art shows a golden sunset or sunrise over a palm-lined river with a fort, which reads as a tropical coast rather than a Deccan winter morning.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-06.png (150,2140)-(800,2540): a sun low on the horizon, palm trees and a warm sky behind the black mare.

minors.description: Duarte's ink-stained fingers are drawn as black blotches scattered across the back of his hand, which reads as a skin disease rather than ink.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-07.png (500,980)-(900,1220): irregular dark spots are spread over the back of the hand and knuckles.

minors.description: The script wants 'Nagoji's eyes, unfocused. He is not in the room.' The eyes are sharp and tightly focused in a sideways glance, which reads as wary or calculating, not far away. There is also a white band about 11px tall inside the bottom of the panel between the art's own border and the page panel border, a double-border defect.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-07.png (230,1250)-(1610,1550). The pixel column at x=800 goes dark to y=1525, then white (about 253) from y=1527 to 1536, then the outer black border at 1537-1539.

minors.description: The script says 'Nagoji chained in his place', back in the 1.1 line. Instead he is alone against a different wall with a pot, a small table and a barred stair-window, and the line of chained men is missing, although 9.3 then shows other prisoners beside him.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-09.png (150,420)-(1000,780): a single figure is chained to a wall ring with no other prisoners in the panel.

minors.description: The whisper passed down the line is lettered in a standard solid speech balloon rather than a whisper balloon, and the torch-lit scene does not match the script's 'leaning heads in the dark'.
minors.evidence: page-09.png panel 3: a solid-outline balloon, 'They are gathering us for transport...', with two lit torches at the upper left.

minors.description: The chapter's closing line, 'Storms do not ask permission', is scripted as 'CAPTION (separate, weighted)', but it uses the same box, font and size as the three captions before it, so it has no extra weight.
minors.evidence: page-09.png panel 4: the bottom-right caption box matches the style of the other three caption boxes.
